event.title: Taco Tuesday
event.description:
Taco Tuesday at V’s Cellar

Taco Tuesday is back and better than ever! 🌮 Every Tuesday, we’re serving up our signature tacos, each bursting with bold, fresh flavors. Whether you’re craving our Al Pastor, the sweet & savory kick of Bulgogi Steak, the spicy tang of Korean Chicken, or the zest of Vegan Asian Ginger, we’ve got something for everyone. Plus, every taco is $1 off all day long!

Taco Tuesday is the perfect excuse to enjoy tacos for lunch, dinner, or a snack in between. Come indulge in your favorite fusion taco creations, and don’t forget: each week brings a new reason to come back for more! Whether you’re a Taco Tuesday regular or it’s your first time, we guarantee you’ll find something you love.

Mark your calendars, grab your friends, and make your Tuesday a little tastier with us!

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it is something that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Savvy Caregiver: October 1 – November 5
event.description:
This online class is for family members caring for a loved one with Alzheimer’s disease or related dementia. The class meets for weekly on Thursdays for six-weeks from October 1st – November 5th from 1:00-3:00. The focus is on improving the practice of caregiving. There is a thorough overview of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia as well as the emotions the caregiver may face, a tool for decision making, and how to deal effectively with family issues. You will learn about the stages and how to use that to help your loved one stay “in the Zone.”

This course provides:

  • Information on ADRD.
  • Knowledge of how dementia affects the person.
  • Ideas for setting up daily care and activities for success.
  • Strategies for figuring out what behaviors mean and how to respond.
  • Tools for decision-making.

This class takes place on Zoom.

To help Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska cover licensing and provider costs, there is a fee for participation. Classes are $140 and pre-registration is required. This fee includes access to all 6 weeks of the course including all educational materials. Financial assistance is available.  Education materials may be picked up in Anchorage or Mat Su or mailed throughout Alaska.

For more information  and to register contact Janice Downing: jdowning@alzalaska.org or 907-864-3408

Space is limited – sign up today!

event.title: Art Links – Connect Virtually, Statewide
event.description:
Come and share the joy of Art Links with us via Zoom on the first Tuesday of every month!

Art Links is a welcoming program for adults who want to have fun, meet new people, and keep their minds active and creative. If you are worried about your memory, a care partner, a person experiencing brain changes, or at risk of social isolation, Art Links is a great way to enjoy art, poetry, music, and meaningful connection in a relaxed, friendly setting. Through a variety of creative activities, Art Links encourages self expression, socialization, and connection. Participants may enjoy:

  • A variety of artistic mediums
  • Poetry, music, and movement
  • Memory rich conversations
  • Creative activities facilitated by ARA staff and local artists

Art Links is free and open to all abilities. No registration is required. Friends and family are welcome to join! For more information, contact Janice Downing at jdowning@alzalaska.org or 907-864-3408.

event.title: Mind Sharpener (Mind Aerobics)
event.description:
Your brain deserves a workout just as much as your body does. Mind Sharpener is a fun, interactive program designed to keep your mind active, flexible, and strong.

This program is perfect for anyone looking to maintain or improve cognitive wellness, stay mentally active, and enjoy the benefits of a stronger, sharper brain. Held on Mondays and Fridays over the course of 12 engaging sessions, you’ll participate in exercises proven to boost six essential areas of cognitive function:

  • Memory – techniques to retain and recall information more effectively
  • Concentration – strategies to sharpen focus and attention
  • Processing Speed – exercises to think and respond more quickly
  • Visual-Spatial Acuity – strengthen awareness and orientation skills
  • Language – build word-finding, comprehension, and communication abilities
  • Problem Solving – practice creative and logical thinking approaches
  • Plus, you’ll enjoy a bonus session exploring ways to continue building brain health long after the program ends.

📌 Registration is required. Email Debbie Chulick at dchulick@alzalaska.org to get registered and for more information.

💲 Cost: $140 to cover materials and provider costs. Financial assistance is available – please reach out if cost is a concern.

Ten Keys to Dementia Risk Reduction: A program for cognitive wellness and resilience.

The Ten Keys to Dementia course offers a practical and empowering look at how everyday lifestyle choices influence brain health, and what you can begin doing today to lower your risk of developing dementia. Across ten focused sessions, participants explore one or two key risk factors at a time, guided by subject matter experts who bring clarity, encouragement, and real-world insight. Personalized coaching helps you set attainable goals and stay on track as you make meaningful changes that support long term wellness. The full program cost is $200.

  • Ten weekly 2-hour classes
  • Gain knowledge, tools, and resources to improve and preserve your memory and cognitive skills
  • Developed from most recent medical research
  • Participants set goals to make changes that they choose
  • Perfect for adults interested in reducing their risk of developing dementia and maintaining brain health.

With questions contact JThomas@alzalaska.org.

event.title: CG101: What Is Lewy Body Dementia?
event.description:
October is Lewy Body Dementia Awareness Month, making it an important time to learn more about this complex and often misunderstood form of dementia.

Join Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska for CG101: What Is Lewy Body Dementia?, an educational class designed to help caregivers, family members, and community members better understand Lewy body dementia. Participants will learn about common signs and symptoms, how Lewy body dementia may differ from other forms of dementia, and what caregivers may experience as the disease progresses. We will also discuss practical approaches for supporting someone living with Lewy body dementia and resources available to families.

Whether you are currently caring for someone with Lewy body dementia, have questions about a diagnosis, or simply want to learn more, this class offers an opportunity to build your knowledge and feel better prepared to provide meaningful support.

This event is free to attend. Register for the class here! Contact Janice Downing for more information at jdowning@alzalaska.org or call 907-746-3413.

event.title: Statewide Caregiver Support Group: Virtual
event.description:
Caregiving can be both deeply meaningful and incredibly challenging. It is common to feel rewarded and overwhelmed at the same time. You may sometimes feel like no one truly understands what you are going through, but you are not alone. We understand, and support is available.

Caregiver Support Groups bring together people with shared experiences to offer encouragement, understanding, and practical insight. These groups provide emotional and social support, a chance to learn what has worked for others, and information about helpful local resources.

Free to attend, this is an online support meeting available statewide in Alaska on the second and fourth Thursday of each month. You may join by phone or Zoom and attend one meeting or continue coming as often as you find helpful.

Caregiving can be deeply meaningful and, at times, incredibly hard. It is normal to feel both fulfilled and overwhelmed. You may sometimes feel like no one truly understands what you are going through, but you are not alone. We are here to listen, and support is available.

Caregiver Support Groups connect people with shared experiences in a welcoming space to offer understanding, encouragement, and practical insight. Participants can share what has helped them, learn from others, and access information about helpful local resources.

This free, in person Caregiver Support Group meets on the second Saturday of each month at the Noel Wien Library in Fairbanks. You are welcome to attend once or return as often as you find helpful.

event.title: Art Links – Fairbanks (in-person)
event.description:
Come and share the joy of Art Links with us in Fairbanks! Art Links is a social support program that promotes engagement for individuals diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias or seniors at risk of isolation and depression. By using a variety of creative art ideas, we promote self-expression as well as socialization and meaningful connections. Participants enjoy:

  • A variety of artistic mediums
  • Music and movement
  • Memory-rich conversations
  • Facilitated by ARA staff and local artists.

Free to attend! No registration required. Share with friends and family. With questions, contact Jennifer Willeford at JWilleford@alzalaska.org or 907-621-6071.

event.description:
Ten Keys to Dementia Risk Reduction: A program for cognitive wellness and resilience.

The Ten Keys to Dementia course offers a practical and empowering look at how everyday lifestyle choices influence brain health, and what you can begin doing today to lower your risk of developing dementia. Across ten focused sessions, participants explore one or two key risk factors at a time, guided by subject matter experts who bring clarity, encouragement, and real-world insight. Personalized coaching helps you set attainable goals and stay on track as you make meaningful changes that support long term wellness. The full program cost is $200.

What to expect:

  • Ten weekly 2-hour classes
  • Gain knowledge, tools, and resources to improve and preserve your memory and cognitive skills
  • Developed from most recent medical research
  • Participants set goals to make changes that they choose
  • Perfect for adults interested in reducing their risk of developing dementia and maintaining brain health.

With questions contact JThomas@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Legal Services Clinic
event.description:
Need help with legal planning? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska’s Legal Service Clinic offers free 30-minute sessions on powers of attorney, wills, bequests, advance directives and other legal services.

Only six spots available each session, reserve yours today by contacting Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org or 907-822-5620.

event.title: Intimate Partner Caregiver Support Group
event.description:

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it issomething that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Savvy Caregiver: October 1 – November 5
event.description:
This online class is for family members caring for a loved one with Alzheimer’s disease or related dementia. The class meets for weekly on Thursdays for six-weeks from October 1st – November 5th from 1:00-3:00. The focus is on improving the practice of caregiving. There is a thorough overview of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementia as well as the emotions the caregiver may face, a tool for decision making, and how to deal effectively with family issues. You will learn about the stages and how to use that to help your loved one stay “in the Zone.”

This course provides:

  • Information on ADRD.
  • Knowledge of how dementia affects the person.
  • Ideas for setting up daily care and activities for success.
  • Strategies for figuring out what behaviors mean and how to respond.
  • Tools for decision-making.

This class takes place on Zoom.

To help Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska cover licensing and provider costs, there is a fee for participation. Classes are $140 and pre-registration is required. This fee includes access to all 6 weeks of the course including all educational materials. Financial assistance is available.  Education materials may be picked up in Anchorage or Mat Su or mailed throughout Alaska.

For more information  and to register contact Janice Downing: jdowning@alzalaska.org or 907-864-3408

Space is limited – sign up today!

event.title: Mind Sharpener (Mind Aerobics)
event.description:
Your brain deserves a workout just as much as your body does. Mind Sharpener is a fun, interactive program designed to keep your mind active, flexible, and strong.

This program is perfect for anyone looking to maintain or improve cognitive wellness, stay mentally active, and enjoy the benefits of a stronger, sharper brain. Held on Mondays and Fridays over the course of 12 engaging sessions, you’ll participate in exercises proven to boost six essential areas of cognitive function:

  • Memory – techniques to retain and recall information more effectively
  • Concentration – strategies to sharpen focus and attention
  • Processing Speed – exercises to think and respond more quickly
  • Visual-Spatial Acuity – strengthen awareness and orientation skills
  • Language – build word-finding, comprehension, and communication abilities
  • Problem Solving – practice creative and logical thinking approaches
  • Plus, you’ll enjoy a bonus session exploring ways to continue building brain health long after the program ends.

📌 Registration is required. Email Debbie Chulick at dchulick@alzalaska.org to get registered and for more information.

event.description:
Experience an extraordinary intergenerational concert unlike any other. One Voice, One Lifetime brings together the voices of elementary, middle, and High School students alongside Alaskans living with Alzheimer’s in a moving celebration of music, memory, and community.

This rare performance transcends cultural, generational, socioeconomic, and religious differences, reminding us that music has the power to unite us all. Through familiar favorites and inspiring new songs, these voices will share a message of hope, connection, and belonging—demonstrating that while memories may fade, the gift of music continues to bring us together.

 

Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska is proud to collaborate with Keys to Life Alaska for the “One Voice, Many Lifetimes” Concert on Sunday, October 18, 2026, from 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM at the Alaska Performing Arts Center, Discovery Theater in Anchorage. This special evening will bring community together through music, reflection, and shared experience. Tickets will be available starting September 15.

event.title: The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace
event.description:
The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace

Join us for our NEW Page Turners Book Club, a welcoming monthly discussion group for anyone interested in brain health, healthy aging, and lifelong learning. Caregiving can be demanding, and it’s easy to put your own interests aside. This book club is an opportunity to slow down, enjoy a good book, and connect with others who understand the caregiving journey. Read at your own pace, then join us each month to share insights, discuss the reading, celebrate successes, talk through challenges, and support one another in a welcoming, judgment free environment.

REGISTER HERE! 

Our first featured book is Aging with Grace by Dr. David Snowdon, the groundbreaking account of the landmark Nun Study, one of the most influential studies on aging and Alzheimer’s disease. Together, we’ll explore what this remarkable research teaches us about cognitive health, resilience, purpose, and the factors that may help support brain health throughout life.

The club meets on the 4th Wednesday of each month from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m., beginning August 26, and is open to participants in Fairbanks and statewide via Zoom.

For our first discussion in August, we’ll cover Chapters 1 through 3. During our September meeting, we’ll discuss 4-6, in October we’ll discuss chapters 7-9, and we’ll close out the book in November with chapters 10-13. We’ll begin a new book club in January with Tangled but Sarah Leavitt – stay tuned for more.

Books are available through Amazon, ThriftBooks, Kindle, and other online retailers. You may also be able to borrow the ebook or audiobook through the Libby app with your local library card or check with the Noel Wien Library or your local library for available copies.

Whether you’re a caregiver, healthcare professional, or simply interested in healthy aging and brain health, we invite you to read, reflect, and connect with us. We look forward to learning and growing together.

Register today via Zoom.

event.description:

Join Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska for CG101: Healthy Body, Healthy Brain, a free, engaging 60 minute program presented in collaboration with the Alzheimer’s Association. This class explores current research and practical strategies for supporting lifelong brain health through everyday choices and habits.

Participants will learn about the connections between brain and body health, including the role of nutrition, physical activity, cognitive engagement, and social connection. The class will also offer practical ideas for incorporating healthy habits into daily life and making positive changes at any age.

Whether you are a caregiver, concerned about your own brain health, supporting someone you love, or simply interested in healthy aging, this class provides useful information and approachable ways to support both your body and your brain.

event.title: The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace
event.description:
The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace

Join us for our NEW Page Turners Book Club, a welcoming monthly discussion group for anyone interested in brain health, healthy aging, and lifelong learning. Caregiving can be demanding, and it’s easy to put your own interests aside. This book club is an opportunity to slow down, enjoy a good book, and connect with others who understand the caregiving journey. Read at your own pace, then join us each month to share insights, discuss the reading, celebrate successes, talk through challenges, and support one another in a welcoming, judgment free environment.

REGISTER HERE! 

Our first featured book is Aging with Grace by Dr. David Snowdon, the groundbreaking account of the landmark Nun Study, one of the most influential studies on aging and Alzheimer’s disease. Together, we’ll explore what this remarkable research teaches us about cognitive health, resilience, purpose, and the factors that may help support brain health throughout life.

The club meets on the 4th Wednesday of each month from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m., beginning August 26, and is open to participants in Fairbanks and statewide via Zoom.

For our first discussion in August, we’ll cover Chapters 1 through 3. During our September meeting, we’ll discuss 4-6, in October we’ll discuss chapters 7-9, and we’ll close out the book in November with chapters 10-13. We’ll begin a new book club in January with Tangled but Sarah Leavitt – stay tuned for more.

Books are available through Amazon, ThriftBooks, Kindle, and other online retailers. You may also be able to borrow the ebook or audiobook through the Libby app with your local library card or check with the Noel Wien Library or your local library for available copies.

Whether you’re a caregiver, healthcare professional, or simply interested in healthy aging and brain health, we invite you to read, reflect, and connect with us. We look forward to learning and growing together.

Register today via Zoom.

event.title: The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace
event.description:
The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace

Join us for our NEW Page Turners Book Club, a welcoming monthly discussion group for anyone interested in brain health, healthy aging, and lifelong learning. Caregiving can be demanding, and it’s easy to put your own interests aside. This book club is an opportunity to slow down, enjoy a good book, and connect with others who understand the caregiving journey. Read at your own pace, then join us each month to share insights, discuss the reading, celebrate successes, talk through challenges, and support one another in a welcoming, judgment free environment.

REGISTER HERE! 

Our first featured book is Aging with Grace by Dr. David Snowdon, the groundbreaking account of the landmark Nun Study, one of the most influential studies on aging and Alzheimer’s disease. Together, we’ll explore what this remarkable research teaches us about cognitive health, resilience, purpose, and the factors that may help support brain health throughout life.

The club meets on the 4th Wednesday of each month from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m., beginning August 26, and is open to participants in Fairbanks and statewide via Zoom.

During our September meeting, we’ll discuss 4-6, in October we’ll discuss chapters 7-9, and we’ll close out the book in November with chapters 10-13. We’ll begin a new book club in January with Tangled but Sarah Leavitt – stay tuned for more.

Books are available through Amazon, ThriftBooks, Kindle, and other online retailers. You may also be able to borrow the ebook or audiobook through the Libby app with your local library card or check with the Noel Wien Library or your local library for available copies.

Whether you’re a caregiver, healthcare professional, or simply interested in healthy aging and brain health, we invite you to read, reflect, and connect with us. We look forward to learning and growing together.

Register today via Zoom.

event.title: The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace
event.description:
The Page Turners Book Club: Aging with Grace

Join us for our NEW Page Turners Book Club, a welcoming monthly discussion group for anyone interested in brain health, healthy aging, and lifelong learning. Caregiving can be demanding, and it’s easy to put your own interests aside. This book club is an opportunity to slow down, enjoy a good book, and connect with others who understand the caregiving journey. Read at your own pace, then join us each month to share insights, discuss the reading, celebrate successes, talk through challenges, and support one another in a welcoming, judgment free environment.

REGISTER HERE! 

Our first featured book is Aging with Grace by Dr. David Snowdon, the groundbreaking account of the landmark Nun Study, one of the most influential studies on aging and Alzheimer’s disease. Together, we’ll explore what this remarkable research teaches us about cognitive health, resilience, purpose, and the factors that may help support brain health throughout life.

The club meets on the 4th Wednesday of each month from 6:00 to 7:30 p.m., beginning August 26, and is open to participants in Fairbanks and statewide via Zoom.

For our first discussion in August, we’ll cover Chapters 1 through 3. During our September meeting, we’ll discuss 4-6, in October we’ll discuss chapters 7-9, and we’ll close out the book in November with chapters 10-13. We’ll begin a new book club in January with Tangled but Sarah Leavitt – stay tuned for more.

Books are available through Amazon, ThriftBooks, Kindle, and other online retailers. You may also be able to borrow the ebook or audiobook through the Libby app with your local library card or check with the Noel Wien Library or your local library for available copies.

Whether you’re a caregiver, healthcare professional, or simply interested in healthy aging and brain health, we invite you to read, reflect, and connect with us. We look forward to learning and growing together.

Register today via Zoom.

event.description:
Come and share the joy of Art Links with us! Art Links is a social support program that promotes engagement for individuals diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias or seniors at risk of isolation and depression. By using a variety of creative art ideas, we promote self-expression as well as socialization and meaningful connections. Participants enjoy:

  • A variety of artistic mediums
  • Music and movement
  • Memory-rich conversations
  • Facilitated by ARA staff and local artists.

Free to attend! No registration required. Share with friends and family. For more information, contact Julie Jordan at jjordan@alzalaska.org or 907-864-3403.

event.title: Intimate Partner Caregiver Support Group
event.description:
Having an intimate partner who has some form of dementia can create challenges that are different from those who are caring for a parent, sibling or other relative or friend.

ARA currently has two separate support groups specifically for caregivers or care partners who are caring for their intimate partners. These groups provide the safe space for partners to share and gain support from others who are learning how to deal with similar challenges.

Questions or ready to sign up? Contact Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Fairbanks Caregiver Support Group
event.description:
Caregiving can be deeply meaningful and, at times, incredibly hard. It is normal to feel both fulfilled and overwhelmed. You may sometimes feel like no one truly understands what you are going through, but you are not alone. We are here to listen, and support is available.

Caregiver Support Groups connect people with shared experiences in a welcoming space to offer understanding, encouragement, and practical insight. Participants can share what has helped them, learn from others, and access information about helpful local resources.

This free, in person Caregiver Support Group meets on the second Saturday of each month at the Noel Wien Library in Fairbanks. You are welcome to attend once or return as often as you find helpful.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it issomething that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

Caregiving can be both deeply meaningful and incredibly challenging. It is common to feel rewarded and overwhelmed at the same time. You may sometimes feel like no one truly understands what you are going through, but you are not alone. We understand, and support is available.

Caregiver Support Groups bring together people with shared experiences to offer encouragement, understanding, and practical insight. These groups provide emotional and social support, a chance to learn what has worked for others, and information about helpful local resources.

Free to attend, this is an online support meeting available statewide in Alaska on the second and fourth Thursday of each month. You may join by phone or Zoom and attend one meeting or continue coming as often as you find helpful.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it is something that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

Caregiving can be both deeply meaningful and incredibly challenging. It is common to feel rewarded and overwhelmed at the same time. You may sometimes feel like no one truly understands what you are going through, but you are not alone. We understand, and support is available.

Caregiver Support Groups bring together people with shared experiences to offer encouragement, understanding, and practical insight. These groups provide emotional and social support, a chance to learn what has worked for others, and information about helpful local resources.

Free to attend, this is an online support meeting available statewide in Alaska on the second and fourth Thursday of each month. You may join by phone or Zoom and attend one meeting or continue coming as often as you find helpful.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it issomething that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

Having an intimate partner who has some form of dementia can create challenges that are different from those who are caring for a parent, sibling or other relative or friend.

ARA currently has two separate support groups specifically for caregivers or care partners who are caring for their intimate partners. These groups provide the safe space for partners to share and gain support from others who are learning how to deal with similar challenges.

Questions or ready to sign up? Contact Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Fairbanks Caregiver Support Group
event.description:
Caregiving can be deeply meaningful and, at times, incredibly hard. It is normal to feel both fulfilled and overwhelmed. You may sometimes feel like no one truly understands what you are going through, but you are not alone. We are here to listen, and support is available.

Caregiver Support Groups connect people with shared experiences in a welcoming space to offer understanding, encouragement, and practical insight. Participants can share what has helped them, learn from others, and access information about helpful local resources.

This free, in person Caregiver Support Group meets on the second Saturday of each month at the Noel Wien Library in Fairbanks. You are welcome to attend once or return as often as you find helpful.

event.title: Art Links – Fairbanks (in-person)
event.description:
Come and share the joy of Art Links with us in Fairbanks! Art Links is a social support program that promotes engagement for individuals diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias or seniors at risk of isolation and depression. By using a variety of creative art ideas, we promote self-expression as well as socialization and meaningful connections. Participants enjoy:

  • A variety of artistic mediums
  • Music and movement
  • Memory-rich conversations
  • Facilitated by ARA staff and local artists.

Free to attend! No registration required. Share with friends and family. With questions, contact Jennifer Willeford at JWilleford@alzalaska.org or 907-621-6071.

event.title: Statewide Caregiver Support Group: Virtual
event.description:
Caregiving can be both deeply meaningful and incredibly challenging. It is common to feel rewarded and overwhelmed at the same time. You may sometimes feel like no one truly understands what you are going through, but you are not alone. We understand, and support is available.

Caregiver Support Groups bring together people with shared experiences to offer encouragement, understanding, and practical insight. These groups provide emotional and social support, a chance to learn what has worked for others, and information about helpful local resources.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it issomething that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Saturday Adventures at the Center: Book Spotlight “Sofia Valdez, Future Prez”
event.venue_json: {"id":34623,"global_id":"www.civilandhumanrights.org?id=34623","venue":"National Center for Civil and Human Rights","address":"100 Ivan Allen Jr. Blvd","city":"Atlanta","country":"United States","state":"GA","zip":"30313","url":"https://www.civilandhumanrights.org/event-space/center-for-civil-and-human-rights-2/","show_map":true,"show_map_link":true}
event.description:
Continue celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month with a special Storytime at the Center. During this engaging program, Center staff will read Sofia Valdez, Future Prez, the inspiring story of a young girl who learns that when something needs to change, anyone can step up and make a difference. event.title: A Worthy Objective: National Teachers Day at the Center
event.venue_json: {"id":266,"global_id":"www.civilandhumanrights.org?id=266","venue":"National Center for Civil and Human Rights","address":"100 Ivan Allen Jr. Blvd","city":"Atlanta","country":"United States","state":"GA","website":"civilandhumanrights.org","url":"https://www.civilandhumanrights.org/event-space/ncchr__trashed/","geo_lat":33.764055,"geo_lng":-84.3930512,"show_map":false,"show_map_link":false}
event.description:
In honor of National Teachers Day, the Center invites educators to enjoy an afternoon of inspiration, exploration, and appreciation. Inspired by Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s belief that education should provide both “the power of concentration” and “worthy objectives on which to concentrate,” this special event offers teachers the opportunity to experience the Center at their own pace while discovering exhibitions, programs, and resources designed to support learning beyond the classroom. 

Throughout the afternoon, the Education Team will spotlight resources available to teachers through facilitated Field Guide experiences and Traveling Trunk demonstrations, providing ideas for bringing civil and human rights education into classrooms and learning spaces. Educators can also participate in art and history activities that celebrate the curiosity and creativity at the heart of great teaching. Whether you’re looking for classroom inspiration, educational tools, or simply an afternoon to explore, we invite you to celebrate the power of education at the Center.

event.title: Saturday Adventures at the Center
event.venue_json: {"id":34623,"global_id":"www.civilandhumanrights.org?id=34623","venue":"National Center for Civil and Human Rights","address":"100 Ivan Allen Jr. Blvd","city":"Atlanta","country":"United States","state":"GA","zip":"30313","url":"https://www.civilandhumanrights.org/event-space/center-for-civil-and-human-rights-2/","show_map":true,"show_map_link":true}
event.description:
Join us this Saturday for an unforgettable experience with interactive storyteller Mama Koku, who will lead high-energy, improvised storytelling sessions at 12 p.m. Known for her magnetic stage presence, Mama Koku transforms storytelling into “story-doing,” inviting children and families to step into the narrative and become part of the performance. Each session is lively, creative, and completely unique, blending imagination, movement, and collaboration in a way that keeps audiences fully engaged.

While you’re here, be sure to explore Change Agent Adventure: Children’s Gallery, an interactive space designed for children 12 and under. This hands-on “secret headquarters” invites kids to play, create, and build confidence as they discover what it means to be a changemaker.

About the Storyteller
Mama Koku is a celebrated teaching artist and storyteller known throughout Metro Atlanta for her dynamic and interactive style. A graduate with honors from North Carolina Central University, she studied theater with concentrations in performance and education. She began her career as a high school theatre teacher, where she honed her work as a storyteller and children’s writer. Her engaging approach has earned her recognition as the Official Teller for the National Black Arts Festival’s Education Village and The Coretta Scott King Book Awards Book Fair. Website: Mama Koku | Watch the Stories Come to Life

event.title: CIVICS 4 ALL AGES!!

The fight for justice, equality, and civic participation belongs to all of us, and it is never too early to begin learning how to make a difference. CIVICS 4 ALL AGES! is a special family learning experience that helps participants better understand how government works, why civic engagement matters, and how individuals can create change in their communities. Through engaging discussions and real-world examples, families will explore the foundations of civics in a welcoming and accessible environment. 

Hosted in the Action Lab and Rotunda, the program is designed for both adults and young learners, with activities tailored to each audience. The experience begins with youth-focused programming that introduces civic concepts through interactive, kid-friendly activities before shifting to sessions designed for adults, allowing every family member to participate and learn. Whether you’re looking to build your civic knowledge, spark meaningful family conversations, or inspire the next generation of changemakers, CIVICS 4 ALL AGES! offers a unique opportunity for the whole family to learn, engage, and grow together.

event.title: National Buy Nothing Day at the Center

The day after Thanksgiving is often known as one of the biggest shopping days of the year, but National Buy Nothing Day invites us to pause and think differently about consumption, community, and the impact of our choices. Join the Center for an afternoon of learning and reflection as we explore how everyday purchasing decisions affect people, communities, and the environment. Through engaging activities and conversations, visitors will gain new perspectives on ethical consumption and discover ways to make more intentional choices. 

In partnership with the Atlanta Tool Bank, guests can participate in special “My Passion” sessions to learn about each organization’s mission and how they help build a more sustainable Atlanta. The event will also feature an ethical footprint-themed art activity, a live artist painting experience, and a donation collection that encourages giving back to the community. Whether you’re interested in reducing waste, rethinking consumer habits, or finding practical ways to make a positive impact, National Buy Nothing Day at the Center offers an inspiring opportunity to explore sustainability, stewardship, and community action.

Fire & Rhône: A Tablas Creek Wine Dinner
Saturday, October 17 | Tasting at 5 PM | Dinner at 6:30 PM
$125 per person + tax & gratuity

Fire, wine and a table meant to be shared.

Join us at Bar, Justa for an evening featuring the Rhône-inspired wines of Tablas Creek Vineyard, presented by National Sales Manager Darren Delmore, alongside a family-style dinner prepared over an open flame.

Located in Paso Robles, California, Tablas Creek is a pioneer of California’s Rhône movement. Founded through a partnership between the Haas family and the Perrin family of Château de Beaucastel in Châteauneuf-du-Pape, the vineyard helped introduce Rhône varieties to California and has become known for combining Southern Rhône tradition with the distinctive terroir of Paso Robles.

Meet Darren Delmore

Joining us for the evening will be Darren Delmore, National Sales Manager for Tablas Creek Vineyard. Darren joined Tablas Creek in 2012 following a wine career that took him through ten harvests across California, Oregon and Australia.

Raised by restaurateurs in San Luis Obispo, Darren took an unconventional route into the wine world, with early chapters in competitive surfing and publishing as an editor at Surfing Magazine. His wine experience has included working with Rhône varieties at Bonny Doon Vineyard, Pinot Noir at Hirsch Vineyards and a harvest at Two Hands in Australia’s Barossa Valley, followed by time as a wine educator for Goldeneye Winery.

His appreciation for Tablas Creek began long before joining the team, with the 2002 vintage of Esprit de Beaucastel. Today, his personal collection includes a consecutive vertical of the flagship blend dating back to 2003, and his writing on wine has appeared in publications including Wine Spectator.

Throughout the evening, Darren will guide guests through the Tablas Creek lineup, sharing the stories, varieties, vineyard philosophy and winemaking behind what’s in the glass.

The Dinner

After the tasting begins at 5 PM, dinner starts at 6:30 PM—and this isn’t a traditional plated wine dinner.

We’re taking things back to the fire with a primal, open-fire cooking experience served family-style. The evening will feature tri-tip, lamb chops and snapper collars cooked over live flame, bringing smoke, char and the unmistakable flavor of fire to the table.

Rather than individual composed courses, expect a communal style of dining, with generous dishes passed around the table and enjoyed alongside the evening’s wines. The complete dinner menu and pairings will be announced as we get closer to the event.

Featured Wines

2024 Vermentino $38.99

From the crisp, saline character of Vermentino and the freshness of Patelin Rosé to varietal Grenache and Mourvèdre and the winery’s flagship Esprit blends, the lineup offers a broad look at what Tablas Creek does best.

A Northern California wine professional with a background spanning winery operations, hospitality, wine education and sustainable agriculture, Andrew brings both deep wine knowledge and an approachable style to the table. Before representing Louis M. Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Color Bash
event.description:
Following the runaway success of Glow-N-Fire — named the Pollstar Family Show of the Year — Color Bash takes the action to a whole new level, transforming the arena into a full-throttle collision of color. Vibrant paint-splattered trucks, bursts of color, and electrifying lighting turn every smash, and crash, into a vivid spectacle the whole family can see, feel, and remember.

When the mischievous Skelesaurus drains all the color from Monster Truck Island, it’s up to the crew of Rhinomite™, Mega Wrex™, Tiger Shark™, Bone Shaker™, and Bigfoot® to win it back — one massive stunt at a time, Every wheelie, jump, donut and freestyle run brings the color roaring back, building to a full-arena burst of light, sound, and pure Monster Truck energy. It’s the show you love, reimagined like you’ve never seen it.

“Color Bash is the most vibrant Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live experience we’ve ever created,” said Ken Hudgens, CEO, Family Entertainment Live. “We took everything fans love about the show — the massive trucks, the jaw-dropping stunts, the can’t-look-away energy — and supercharged it with color. It’s a brand-new way to experience the action live, and we can’t wait to bring it to families in [CITY] in 2027.”

Unlike several contemporaries, who’s Top 40 radio-friendly songs were written in English and performed with contemporary instruments, The Mākaha Sons of Niʻihau celebrated Hawai’i and its language in both arrangements and vocal styling. Their dedication to hana kuʻuna, traditional works, has ignited and inspired generations of performers to embrace the journey.

Though the group has evolved through the ensuing five decades – most notably with the loss of Skippy and the departure of Israel – the core members have shared the stage with both minted members and guest artists in live and recorded performances. With Israel’s 1993 departure for his solo career, the group’s name changed to The Mākaha Sons, but the music stayed true to the group’s core principles.

JO KOY BIOGRAPHY 2026
As one of today’s premiere stand-up comedians, Jo Koy has come a long way from his modest beginnings performing in a Las Vegas coffee house. Jo’s uniquely relatable comedy pulls inspiration from his colorful family that has reached all kinds of people and has translated into sold-out arenas around the world.

The comedian continues to be one of the top 10 grossing stand-up comedians each year according to Pollstar and Billboard. Today, he continues selling out and breaking sales records at some of the most prestigious venues around the world including Mall of Asia Arena (Manila, PH), The Forum (Los Angeles), Coca-Cola Arena (Dubai), ICC Theatre (Sydney, AU), O2 Arena (London), Madison Square Garden (New York City), and American Airlines Arena (Dallas) to name a few. In 2022, Koy kicked off his Funny Is Funny World Tour by selling-out the Climate Pledge Arena (over 14,000 tickets) in his hometown of Seattle and ended the tour with a sold-out show at Tacoma Dome (over 19,000 tickets). In 2017, Koy broke a record for the most tickets sold by a single artist at 23,000 tickets and 11 sold-out shows at The Neal S. Blaisdell Concert Hall in Honolulu. In response, the mayor’s office in Honolulu proclaimed November 24th as “Jo Koy Day.”

Koy starred in the 2022 Universal Picture comedy Easter Sunday, the film takes place around a struggling single father that returns to his hometown of Daly City, CA to survive a chaotic Easter with his family. The film is a love letter to his Filipino roots and is loosely based on Jo Koy’s life experiences and stand-up comedy. Easter Sunday was produced by Steven Spielberg’s production company Amblin Partners and is the first motion picture film to feature an all-Filipino cast and be produced by a major studio. In honor of the film, Daly City gave Jo the Keys To The City and declared July 22nd “Jo Koy Day.”

In 2023, Koy appeared in Disney’s Haunted Mansion and voiced characters in Netflix’s animated films, Monkey King and Leo. In 2024, he was most recently heard voicing the character Monkey King in the Paramount+ film, The Tiger’s Apprentice. He’s also appeared in Netflix’s Mr. Iglesias and Comedy Central’s Awkwafina Is Nora from Queens.

In 2023, it was announced that he inked a two-special deal with Netflix with the first special releasing in 2024. Jo returned to Netflix in typical style, sharing his unfiltered opinions on social media, aging and moving into a new phase of his life; his zaddy phase. Filmed at the historic King’s Theatre in Brooklyn, NY, Jo Koy: Live From Brooklyn premiered globally on June 4th, 2024 only on Netflix and reached the Top 10 within the first week. His other Netflix stand-up specials include Live From The Los Angeles Forum, Comin’ In Hot and Live From Seattle. Overall, Koy has had seven highly rated and successful specials on Comedy Central and Netflix. In June 2020, the comedian released his first variety special, Jo Koy: In His Elements on Netflix in which Koy brings the laughs and beats to Manila, spotlighting local culture in a one-of-a-kind show featuring Filipino-American comedians, DJs and B-boys.

On March 21st, 2026, Koy alongside Gabriel “Fluffy” Iglesias will become the first to headline and sell-out SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles for their One Night Only! show.

Koy continues to push for representation in Hollywood and shine a light on Filipino talent. Last year Koy joined Nurse Unseen, a documentary from Emmy-winning director Michele Josue, as an executive producer. The film explores the little-known history and humanity of the unsung Filipino nurses who risked their lives on the frontlines of the COVID-19 pandemic while facing a resurgence of anti-Asian hate in the streets.

In honor of Koy’s impact on Hollywood and comedy, his legacy was permanently cemented during a hand and footprint ceremony at the TCL Chinese Theatre on February 11, 2026, joining an elite group of distinguished talent.

In 2023, Jo came on as a producer for the David Byrne-Fatboy Slim musical, Here Lies Love. Here Lies Love told the story of Imelda Marcos’ rise to power and subsequent fall at the hands of the Philippine People Power Revolution. The show received four Tony Award nominations during its run and was the first to feature an all-Filipino cast on Broadway.

In 2022, Koy was once again acknowledged for his advocacy for more representation in entertainment and was given the proclamation in Los Angeles that October 7th would be declared “Jo Koy Day.”

In 2021, Koy released his first autobiography, Mixed Plate: Chronicles of an All-American Combo with Harper Collins Publishers to raved reviews. In this funny and moving memoir, Koy uncovers the stories behind his stand-up: the conflict, the drama and the laughter as he struggles to find his place in the entertainment industry, his home and around the world.

Jo is currently on his Jo Koy: Just Being Koy Tour.

MAMMA MIA! 

A mother. A daughter. 3 possible dads.
And a trip down the aisle you’ll never forget!

Set on a Greek island paradise where the sun always shines, a tale of love, friendship, and identity is beautifully told through the timeless hits of ABBA. On the eve of her wedding, a daughter’s quest to discover the father she’s never known brings three men from her mother’s past back to the island they last visited decades ago.

For over 25 years, people all around the world have fallen in love with the characters, the story, and the music that make MAMMA MIA! the ultimate feel-good show.
